pages.title: Spice of Life: Onion
pages.text: Spice of Life: Onion is a food variety mod that independently tracks food history and rewards eating a diverse diet. It works alongside Nourished rather than replacing it — both systems run simultaneously and reinforce the same core goal: $(bold)eat variety, not repetition$().

pages.title: How They Interact
pages.text:
Both mods track food history, but they do so independently:

$(bold)Nourished$() tracks variety at the item, family, and group level and applies it as a nutrition multiplier.
$(bold)Spice of Life$() tracks a rolling history of unique foods eaten and grants rewards for diversity.

Eating a varied diet satisfies both systems at once — the same rotation that maximizes Nourished efficiency also earns SoL rewards.

pages.title: Diminishing Returns & SoL
pages.text:
Nourished's diminishing returns and SoL's food history are separate counters. A food that is $(#e05252)saturated$() in Nourished (low nutrition multiplier) may still count as a $(#52c252)new entry$() in SoL's history if you have not eaten it recently.

This means you can strategically eat a wider range of foods to top up SoL's diversity counter while also rotating Nourished families — they reward the same behaviour.

pages.title: Practical Advice
pages.text:
With both mods installed, the optimal strategy is simply to eat as many $(bold)different foods$() as possible each day rather than defaulting to a small rotation.

Instead of eating bread + apple + steak every day, try rotating through 10–15 different foods across the week. Both mods reward this heavily — Nourished via freshness bonuses and SoL via its diversity rewards.
